subject: Security exhibit: sampling guardrails, staging access, and evidence cadence (Cardia Health)
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <m.garcia@cardiahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cardiahealth.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Cardia Health — security exhibit questions (SOC 2 sampling & pen test access)

Hi Soojin / Karthik,

Thanks for sending the MSA + Order Form. Our legal and InfoSec teams reviewed the security exhibit and had a couple of open items before we can move to signature:

1) Sampling bands for SOC 2 evidence: we need confirmation of the sample size you expect for tenant-level audits (e.g., 1%, 5%, or fixed sample sets) and whether samples will be tenant-scoped or cross-tenant aggregated.

2) Pen test access window: we need clarity on the minimum notice period for scheduled penetration tests and whether you allow ephemeral staging credentials (we prefer timebound jumpbox access over long-lived creds).

3) Data minimization during evidence pulls: our security policy requires scoping to the minimum data necessary and a redaction plan if production data is involved.

4) Staging environment parity: the SOC 2 assertions say staging is representative — can you confirm whether staging will contain copies of PHI-like metadata or if that is scrubbed?

Could you propose an evidence cadence (how often you’ll share SOC 2 artifacts and a pen-test readiness window) and a pragmatic set of guardrails we can use in the Order Form? We want to avoid lengthy redlines but need operational clarity to satisfy our auditors.

Appreciate a short playbook rather than legalese — our InfoSec lead (cc'd) will triage.

Best,
Maria Garcia
Senior Counsel, Cardia Health
Maria.Garcia@cardiahealth.com

---
Attachment: request-summary-cardia.pdf (stub — summary of Cardia's questions)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <m.garcia@cardiahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cardia Health — security exhibit questions (SOC 2 sampling & pen test access)

Maria — thanks for the clear ask. I drafted an operational playbook with suggested guardrails and attached a cleaner Exhibit v2 for your review. Key points up front: 

- SOC 2 sampling: we propose a two-track approach: (a) tenant-bounded samples for high-sensitivity customers (default 1% of resources or minimum 5 samples), and (b) aggregated sampling for lower-sensitivity tenants (default 5% or minimum 15 samples). We call these "Bounded" vs "Aggregate" sampling in the playbook.
- Pen test notice: standard is 14 calendar days for scheduled tests; for emergency research (e.g., approved red-teaming) we can accommodate 72 hours with mutual escalation. Ephemeral staging credentials are supported; we provide timeboxed jumpbox accounts and short-lived API tokens for the test window.
- Evidence minimization: we will provide scoped exports and a redaction checklist. For production-affecting pulls we require a joint data-handling plan signed by both parties.
- Staging parity: staging mirrors infra but by default we scrub PHI/PII fields; customers can opt into a closer parity model with stronger safeguards (e.g., KMS-backed keys and monitored access).

I'm attaching security-exhibit-draft_v2.docx and a pen-test-scope-chart.xlsx that maps sample bands to test types and a proposed handback cadence (weekly runbook for first 3 months, then monthly snapshots).

If that looks good, we can (1) accept high-level guardrails in the Order Form, (2) add a short operational SOW that references the playbook for runbook-level details, and (3) surface any carve-outs in the MSA appendix.

Next steps I propose: short call early next week with your InfoSec lead -> we capture any carve-outs, then Karthik and Laura will produce the minimal redline to the Order Form.

Thanks — attaching the draft.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Assurance Programs, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: security-exhibit-draft_v2.docx; pen-test-scope-chart.xlsx

Subject: Re: Cardia Health — security exhibit questions (SOC 2 sampling & pen test access)

Thanks, Soojin — the playbook is helpful. A few requested edits from InfoSec after a quick read: 

- Sampling floor: Cardia insists on a hard minimum of 10 tenant-bounded samples for any tenant with PHI/regulated data (we can accept your 1% rule as long as the minimum is 10).
- Encryption and key control: please add explicit wording that any staging parity with real data uses KMS-backed keys managed by Cardia, or, if Redwood manages keys, that Cardia must be notified of any crypto key access events during the evidence window.
- Evidence retention: our auditors expect retained artifacts for 18 months; we can mirror Redwood's retention if you can demonstrate encryption and access logs.

Please see inline comments on your Exhibit v2 (forwarded below). If we can get those three bullets addressed (or operationally documented in the SOW with stronger monitoring), Cardia's legal team can sign off on the exhibit and proceed to Order Form sign-off.

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <m.garcia@cardiahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cardia Health — security exhibit questions (SOC 2 sampling & pen test access)

Maria — appreciate the quick review and clear asks. Replying to close the loop and propose contract language and operational next steps: 

1) Sampling floor: we will adopt Cardia's request for a hard minimum of 10 tenant-bounded samples when the customer declares regulated data in the Order Form. Language we propose to add to the Exhibit: "For tenants that have been designated as handling regulated data, Redwood will provide tenant-bounded samples with a minimum floor of 10 items per audit event."

2) Encryption/key control: we will add a technical appendix to the SOW describing KMS options: (a) Customer-managed keys (recommended for Cardia) where Cardia controls tenant KMS and Redwood documents access logs, or (b) Redwood-managed keys with real-time notifications to a Cardia security webhook and logged key events. We'll link to the key-access runbook in Appendix B.

3) Evidence retention: Redwood can commit to 18 months retention for audit artifacts related to the tenant, provided the artifacts are stored encrypted and access is logged to the customer's audit trail. We'll add a clause: "Audit artifacts will be retained for 18 months and access to artifacts will be logged and available on request for audit purposes."

Operational asks: can you confirm (a) whether Cardia will sign the SOW operational runbook referencing Appendix B, and (b) who on your InfoSec team will be the primary contact for the 14-day pen-test scheduling window? If we have those two confirmations we will prepare a concise redline to the Order Form that accepts the majority of your edits and surfaces the SOW for the detailed controls.

I'll prepare the redline and send by EOD tomorrow for Laura to route through Legal.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
